atlantis-reef.name: Santorini pinnacles
atlantis-reef.text: About 150 m on a bearing of 145°magnetic from the western pillar, there is another somewhat lower pinnacle, rising to 10 m depth.

blue-flame-reef/south-pinnacles.name: Blue Flame East Pinnacle
blue-flame-reef/south-pinnacles.text: There are no reports available on this area.

boat-rock.name: Festival Pinnacle
boat-rock.text: A compact pinnacle and patch of reef south of Boat Rock, across a small sand gap. The pinnacle is a fairly large granite outcrop, about 20 m long, rising from a sand bottom at 18 m to just above 12 m.

canyon.name: Canyon south pinnacle
canyon.text: The south pinnacle comes up to 22 m

coral-gardens-oudekraal/colins-pinnacle.name: Coral Gardens Offshore Pinnacle - 4 m pinnacle
Coral Gardens Offshore Pinnacle - 7 m pinnacle
Coral Gardens Offshore Pinnacle - 10 m pinnacle

coral-gardens-oudekraal/inshore-pinnacle.name: Coral Gardens western cove entry point

finlays-point.name: Finlay's Point Swimthroughs
finlays-point.text: To the north of the point is a group of 3 big boulders which extend above the water near the shore entry point.

justins-caves.name: Justin's Caves swimthrough
justins-caves.text: Shoreward entrance to the main cave

kalk-bay-harbour-wall.name: Kalk Bay Reef
kalk-bay-harbour-wall.text: This is the sandstone reef off the point to the south of the harbour.

mv-daeyang-family.name: MV Daeyang Family - not a lifeboat wreck
mv-daeyang-family.text: There is the relatively intact wreck of an 18 m long vessel with a relatively large deck opening to the east of the main wreckage, which was thought to be a lifeboat, but further investigations suggest that it is more likely a lighter or barge, considerably older than the Daeyang Family, and wrecked previously.

percys-hole.name: Percy's Hole swimthrough
percys-hole.text: The swimt-hrough is a gully with a few very large boulders wedged into the top, covering a spacious swim-through with a bottom of small rounded boulders, which can be reached from both the gully entry and the north entry, with roughly equal convenience, as it is about half way between then.

percys-hole.name: Percy's Hole cave
percys-hole.text: The cave is most easily reached from the north entry, as a surface swim, as it is at the north end of the second gully from the east on the north side of the cove.

percys-hole.name: Percy's Hole high reef offshore end
percys-hole.text: This is easily accessible by boat. Just drop in at the mark. For shore access it is a moderately long swim and usually a waypoint on a swim round the high reef, often via the tunnel swim-through.

photographers-reef.name: JJM Junior reef
photographers-reef.text: This is a low reef about 30 m across the sand to the south of Photographer's. It is about 8.5 m deep on top, and is fairly flat, with no spectacular features. The area is similar to Photographer's Reef.

photographers-reef.name: North Photographer's Reef
photographers-reef.text: A low reef to the north. It is also relatively flat and rises gradually from about 13 m on the sand to about 9 m at the shallowest point.

photographers-reef.name: Compass Reef
photographers-reef.text: The reef to the south west is "Compass Reef", and it is mostly relatively low and made up of a number of quite small outcrops, except for a section of fairly high reef at the west side of the area, this extends up from the sand bottom at about 8 to 9 m to shallower than 6 m.

pie-rock-and-outer-castle-reefs/east-pie.name: East Pie Rock Reef, Eastern pinnacle
pie-rock-and-outer-castle-reefs/east-pie.text: Top at 12 m, a small cluster of tall pinnacles with deep cracks between them, with sand edge nearby to the northeast at about 24 to 24 m.

rocky-bay.name: Gully entry point for shore dive
rocky-bay.text: Shore dive from the gully: Park on the verge of the seaward side of the road above the inlet to the north east of the resort at Steenbras River mouth. It is quite a hike down to water, but not difficult.

smits-reef/batsata-maze.name: Maze Cave
smits-reef/batsata-maze.text: Main entrance to the cave swim-through

ss-oakburn-and-bos-400.name: BOS 400
ss-oakburn-and-bos-400.text: On the north shore of Duiker Point.

whittle-rock/northwest-pinnacle.name: Cathedral Pinnacle
whittle-rock/northwest-pinnacle.text: A large boulder, 18 m deep on top, at the end of a small ridge overlooking a small sandy strip with scattered small boulders on the northern slope of the main reef.

whittle-rock/northwest-pinnacle.name: Kelly's anchor
whittle-rock/northwest-pinnacle.text: A large iron anchor without a stock at about 32 m depth, on boulders and sand, north part of the main reef.

whittle-rock/northwest-pinnacle.name: Riaan and Sven's anchor
whittle-rock/northwest-pinnacle.text: On the main reef, said to be about 20 m east of the mark at 18 m depth, described as unusually large.

whittle-rock/northwest-pinnacle.name: September anchor
whittle-rock/northwest-pinnacle.text: A large iron anchor at 15 m depth on the northwestern ridge of the main reef.

whittle-rock/northwest-pinnacle.name: Little anchor
whittle-rock/northwest-pinnacle.text: A smaller iron anchor on the main reef, at 18 m depth.

whittle-rock/whittle-rock.name: Northeastern Pinnacle and Euphrates Gully area
JJ's anchor
whittle-rock/whittle-rock.text: A large anchor with iron stock at 17 m depth, on the Euphrates Rise.

whittle-rock/whittle-rock.name: Billy's anchor
whittle-rock/whittle-rock.text: A large anchor "much like the Euphtrates anchors" on the Euphrates Rise, at 19 m depth. This is quite close to JJ's anchor, so it is possible they are the same anchor, but far enough for doubt.

whittle-rock/whittle-rock.name: Euphrates anchor (west)
whittle-rock/whittle-rock.text: At about 24 m depth, on rocky bottom.

whittle-rock/whittle-rock.name: Euphrates anchor (central)
whittle-rock/whittle-rock.text: At about 25 m depth, on sand

whittle-rock/whittle-rock.name: Euphrates anchor (east)
whittle-rock/whittle-rock.text: At about 25 m depth, on sand

whittle-rock/whittle-rock.name: Marc's anchor
whittle-rock/whittle-rock.text: A large iron anchor without a stock lying flat at 14.5 m depth on the flat rock of the main reef, near the 5 m pinnacle, and well camouflaged by encrusting growth.

whittle-rock/shards-cluster.name: Victor's chain
whittle-rock/shards-cluster.text: A length of heavy open link mooring chain on the northeastern slope between The Shards and the Euphrates rise at a depth range of approximately 20 to 23 m.

whittle-rock/west-pinnacle.name: Bruce's anchor
whittle-rock/west-pinnacle.text: A small steel anchor, firmly stuck in a small space between a few large boulders at the north side of the Eastern Sand Tongue at a depth of about 24 m. Not easy to see unless you swim right over it.

whittle-rock/southeast-pinnacle.name: Southeast pinnacle chain (Neptune's bath plug)
whittle-rock/southeast-pinnacle.text: A heavy, slightly dished, metal disc, somewhat less than a metre in diameter, with a central lug shackled to the end of a length of heavy chain, known as Neptune's bathplug, on the sand on the north side of the big Eastern Sand Tongue.

whittle-rock/table-top-pinnacle.name: Table Top anchor
whittle-rock/table-top-pinnacle.text: A small anchor at the base of the Table Top pinnacle on the southwest side, near the sandy strip, at approximately 26 m

windmill-offshore-reefs/windmill-offshor.name: SUEX Reef
windmill-offshore-reefs/windmill-offshor.text: A long, narrow pair of straight parallel ridges with a narrow strip of sand between them. Not very high, but with a couple of higher boulders or outcrops. Fairly unmistakable appearance.
